tremely cost-effective, at $15 to $30 per DALY
gained. In light of this cost-effectiveness and the
burden of disease addressed, the Rockefeller
Foundation and the UNDP are initiating a major
program to document and explore the potential of

Mass screening and referral
Mass screening for disease control involves the ex-
amination of asymptomatic individuals to identify
and treat those affected by disease. Although this
method has been used to control some infectious
diseases, such as tuberculosis, it is mostly used
for noncommunicable diseases. Mass screening
makes sense for highly prevalent diseases that can
